note: One order-independent rule set for GLM-5.2 NVFP4 under SGLang, pure TP4. It is NOT derived from the vLLM pack next door: `label transfer` requires structural equality and these are two kernel vocabularies for the same model. Only 11 of that pack's 33 name fragments appear in an SGLang capture at all, and all 11 are ambiguous prefixes whose disambiguating neighbours are absent -- so it was rewritten from the folded program rather than migrated. The same two checks hold the same property as the vLLM pack: `subsumptions` proves order-dependence from the rule file alone, `disagreements` observes it against a real capture. Both are in `alignment/labeling/rules.py`; both are zero here.
provenance: Generated by `scripts/build_sglang_label_rules.py` from the run's own cost manifest, so a suffix naming a slot the model does not emit fails loudly instead of silently claiming nothing. The script is the editable form; this file is its output. Capture: logs/20260828_0_glm52_nvfp4_pure_tp_sglang_alignment/profile_nsys (10707 iterations, 84.7 M kernel rows, SGLang @ 402eaff45 on B200 x4).
how_rules_were_written: Every position rule was read off a printed decoder-layer body, not guessed from a kernel name. `alignment/labeling/README.md` records why: naming a CUTLASS tile by its shape once inflated this model's measured q_absorb by 88% and manufactured a 2x underestimate that did not exist. Three rules that WERE written that way here were caught and corrected the same way -- see `corrected`.
corrected: The router GEMM was charged to `attention.fused_qkv_a_proj`: both collectives are spelled `flashinfer::trtllm_allreduce_fusion`, so `after_name` cannot separate the attention-side one from the MoE-side one. Restated on `after` (the preceding OPERATION) the two never collide.

`main.lm_head` was keyed on 'a split-K GEMM after an RMSNorm', which the indexer's key projection also is -- `kv_a_rms_norm` shares the mangled RMSNormKernel spelling with the final norm. The rule fired in all 78 layers and never once on the head.

The dense ragged MHA prefill path (M6) had its GEMM pair inverted: SGLang materializes full K/V through `kv_b_proj` BEFORE that kernel, so the GEMM after it is the output projection, not a value up-projection.
one_to_many: Four operations claim slots beyond their own, because SGLang runs one launch where the model keeps two steps. Each is stated at its rule in the generator with the source line that establishes the fusion: q_b_proj+q_absorb (one GEMM between the KV latent norm and the RoPE, on every track of every sequence), main_rope+query_concat (`mla_rope_quantize_fp8` packs nope+pe itself), mla_cache_append+index_remap (M2: `use_fused_topk` drops the page table out of the top-k transform), and tp_allreduce_residual_norm+tp_allreduce. The last is not a fusion but a branch: `eval_atomic_or_zero` in `simulator/src/arch/glm52_sglang_nvfp4_tp_dsa_moe.rs:815-835` zeroes one of the two on a single `use_fused` predicate, so one measured kernel claiming both cannot double-count -- and it turns a real divergence (the model leaves the fused path above 2730 tokens, SGLang does not) from invisible unmapped time into a ratio on one operation row.

windows.note: Folded positions, not launches: the inventory folds `exact_contiguous_repeat`, so one position stands for every launch of that program point. Coverage percentages below are duration-weighted and come from `alignment label coverage`, which is the number acceptance reads.

unmapped_note: The positions that stay unmapped are host-side bookkeeping SGLang runs around the forward -- `at::native::*_elementwise_kernel`, `cub::DeviceScan*`, `compute_position_kernel` -- which the model has no slot for because they are not model work. They are 0.24% of measured GPU time on the 400-iteration window.
